title: Wage-Record Relief Share for Employer Benefit Charging Protests
content:
Under Employer Benefit Charging, charges reached on a wage-record ground are taken at the wage-record relief share: the whole when the amended wage reports the employer filed within the last twelve months number at least four, one half when they number one to three, and zero when it has filed no amended wage report in that time.

A wage-record ground is a protest ground that disputes the employer's base-period wages or its base-period status — that the employer paid the claimant no base-period wages, or that the base-period wages charged to it are wrong.

## The terms in figures

- At least 4 amended wage reports filed in the last 12 months: the wage-record relief share is 1.00, the whole.
- From 1 to 3 amended wage reports: 0.50, one half.
- No amended wage report in that time: 0.00, zero.

## Which reports count

The employer's amended quarterly contribution and wage reports, as filed on its Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts record, each report counted once by its filed date; original and final reports do not count. The twelve months are counted back from the day the protest is decided: a report counts while fewer than twelve whole months separate its filed date from that day — decided on 10 October, a report filed on 11 October of the previous year counts and one filed on 10 October of the previous year does not.

## Boundary pairs (hypothetical)

- 3 amended reports: 0.50. 4 amended reports: 1.00.
- 0 amended reports: 0.00. 1 amended report: 0.50.
- $2,000.00 of charges reached on a wage-record ground with 2 amended reports in the twelve months are taken at 0.50, giving $1,000.00.
